stories.headline: Wall Street snaps losing streak: S&P 7,666.60, Dow +295 as tech leads
stories.dek: Nasdaq +0.5%. Nvidia rose more than 3%. Oil and yields steadier than Tuesday.
stories.caveman: Wednesday was a bounce day. The S&P 500 rose 35.13 points, or 0.5%, to 7,666.60. The Dow gained 295.07 points, or 0.6%, to 53,061.95. The Nasdaq rose 118.05 points, or 0.5%, to 26,217.83. Big tech helped after a rough start to the week. Simple talk: prices went up a bit after two hard days, but the week is still slightly down.
stories.why_it_matters: Taipei morning futures watch U.S. closes. A calmer Wall Street night softens the hangover for Asia chip names.
stories.camps: Bulls say Nvidia strength shows AI demand is alive. Hawks say oil war risk is not gone. People with 401(k)s feel every bounce.

terms.explain: Basket of 500 big U.S. companies. Many treat it as 'the market.'
Index of 30 big U.S. industrial and consumer companies.
U.S. stock index heavy on tech.
Several days in a row when prices fall.

stories.image_alt: Wall Street trading floor or market screens

stories.headline: Oil holds high ground: Brent $95.63, WTI about $91 as Iran fight continues
stories.dek: Brent +1%, WTI +0.9% Wednesday. Less wild than Tuesday’s jump, still expensive.
stories.caveman: Crude did not explode higher again, but it stayed pricey. Brent settled up about 1% at $95.63 a barrel. U.S. oil (WTI) climbed about 0.9% to settle near $91.01. The U.S.–Iran fight kept a war premium in the price. Simple talk: fuel math still hurts even on a 'quiet' oil day.
stories.why_it_matters: Taiwan imports almost all oil. High Brent feeds gasoline, freight, and factory costs.
stories.camps: Energy traders watch Hormuz risk. Peace hopes want a ceasefire. Drivers feel pump prices first.

terms.explain: Main global oil price, dollars per barrel.
Main U.S. oil price.
Official end-of-day futures price.
Extra price traders add when fighting might block oil ships.

stories.image_alt: Oil market or energy industry scene

stories.headline: NY Fed’s Williams: wait-and-see on September hike; 10-year eases to 4.78%
stories.dek: Says no clear sign yet that policy must tighten more. Points to strong AI-led economy.
stories.caveman: New York Fed President John Williams told CNBC he needs more data before deciding if rates must rise on Sept. 15–16. He said there are 'no clear signs right now' that current policy is enough — or that more hikes are required. He blamed higher Treasury yields mostly on a strong U.S. outlook fueled by AI and data-center spending. The 10-year yield slipped to about 4.78% from 4.79%. Simple talk: one big Fed voice said 'not sure yet,' and bond fear cooled a little.
stories.why_it_matters: Mortgage and loan rates track the 10-year. Fed guesses move stocks from Taipei to New York.
stories.camps: Hawks still price a hike. Doves hear wait-and-see. Home buyers watch weekly.

terms.explain: The overnight interest rate the Fed targets. Banks and loans follow it.
The Fed committee that votes on rate moves.
Interest rate on a U.S. government bond. When it rises, loans often get costlier.
Policymaker language for 'I need more data before I vote.'

stories.image_alt: John Williams interview or Fed building

stories.headline: Chevron says it will expand Venezuela operations amid oil squeeze
stories.dek: Shares edged up Wednesday as traders weighed Middle East risk vs. new supply paths.
stories.caveman: AP’s market wrap noted Chevron edged about 0.3% higher after confirming it will expand operations in Venezuela. That detail landed while Brent stayed near $96 and U.S.–Iran fighting kept supply nerves high. Simple talk: when one oil door looks risky, companies try other doors — even messy ones.
stories.why_it_matters: More barrels from anywhere can cool prices later. Politics and sanctions still decide if those barrels really ship.
stories.camps: Energy bulls like new output. Human-rights critics watch Venezuela deals. Drivers just want cheaper fuel.

terms.explain: South American country with huge oil reserves and heavy politics.
Rules that limit trade with a country or company.
A route or country that can send oil to buyers.
A very large oil and gas company.

stories.headline: Broadcom beats Q3, guides soft Q4; CEO sees AI revenue $115B in FY2027
stories.dek: Revenue $29.59B, adjusted EPS $3.32. Q4 sales guide $34.8B vs ~$35.03B expected.
stories.caveman: Broadcom reported a strong fiscal third quarter: about $29.59 billion in sales and $3.32 adjusted earnings per share, both above Wall Street guesses. Semiconductor sales more than tripled. But fourth-quarter revenue guidance of $34.8 billion missed the ~$35.03 billion estimate, so the stock wobbled. CEO Hock Tan still painted a huge AI future — about $115 billion AI revenue in fiscal 2027, then maybe $230 billion in 2028. Simple talk: today good, next-quarter map a bit short, long-term map still huge.
stories.why_it_matters: Broadcom builds custom AI chips for Google, Meta, OpenAI and others. Its guidance moves the whole AI supply chain.
stories.camps: Bulls hear $115B. Bears hear the Q4 miss. Taiwan fabs and board makers watch order timing.

terms.explain: Profit per share after removing some one-time items. Wall Street compares this number.
What a company says it expects to sell or earn next quarter.
A chip built for one big customer’s AI jobs, not sold to everyone.
A company’s own 12-month counting year, not always the calendar year.

stories.headline: Tan: Jalapeño shipping for OpenAI; Gen-2 near tapeout; Anthropic wants more TPUs
stories.dek: Broadcom call details OpenAI, Google, Meta custom silicon roadmaps.
stories.caveman: On the earnings call, Hock Tan said Jalapeño shipments for OpenAI continue, and OpenAI is getting ready to tape out a second-generation chip while planning a third with Broadcom. He talked up faster Google Ironwood TPU shipments to Anthropic and TPU 8i chips to Google, plus Meta MTIA accelerators for inference. Anthropic could deploy about 5 gigawatts of TPU 8i in 2027, with a line of sight to more. Simple talk: the AI labs are ordering factories’ worth of special chips, not just a few servers.
stories.why_it_matters: Gigawatts of chips mean power, HBM memory, packaging, and Taiwan capacity all get squeezed harder.
stories.camps: Cloud labs race to lock supply. Nvidia remains a partner, not gone. Utilities worry about electricity.

terms.explain: OpenAI’s custom inference chip built with Broadcom.
The moment a chip design is finished and sent to the factory to make masks.
Google’s home-made AI accelerator chips.
A huge unit of electric power. AI campuses now get measured this way.

stories.image_alt: AI chip or data center hardware

stories.headline: Apple deepens Broadcom chip pact for U.S. production and AI silicon
stories.dek: Renewed multiyear supply deal cited on Broadcom’s quarter; wireless plus custom AI parts.
stories.caveman: During Broadcom’s quarter, Apple was called out for planning to spend more with Broadcom on U.S. chip production. Analyst notes describe a renewed supply agreement running toward 2031 that covers wireless parts and custom chips likely tied to Apple’s AI plans. Simple talk: Apple wants more control over AI hardware and is writing bigger checks to a key chip partner.
stories.why_it_matters: Apple’s private cloud and device AI need silicon. That demand hits the same foundry and packaging lines everyone else wants.
stories.camps: Apple bulls like vertical control. Broadcom bulls like another anchor customer. Privacy fans watch on-device AI promises.

terms.explain: Chips designed for one company’s products.
Apple’s plan to run some AI jobs in its own cloud with strong privacy rules.
A Broadcom wireless filter part used in phones.
A factory that makes chips designed by other companies.

stories.headline: Nvidia jumps more than 3% and helps lift Wednesday’s tech rebound
stories.dek: AP: chip giant led gains as Wall Street snapped a multi-day slide.
stories.caveman: Nvidia rose more than 3% on Wednesday, helping the Dow and Nasdaq climb after a soft start to September. Traders treated the move as a sign that AI hardware demand still has buyers even while oil and rate fears linger. Simple talk: the biggest AI chip name had a green day, and the whole tech neighborhood felt better.
stories.why_it_matters: Nvidia sets the mood for Taiwan’s GPU, CoWoS, and server chain every night.
stories.camps: Bulls buy dips. Skeptics say one day does not fix war-oil risk. Supply-chain workers watch overnight futures.

terms.explain: U.S. company that makes the most famous AI training GPUs.
Graphics chip now widely used to train and run AI models.
Prices bounce up after falling.
A very large semiconductor company.

stories.image_alt: Stock market screens highlighting tech shares

stories.headline: U.S. and Iran trade biggest barrages since July; Tehran hits Gulf bases
stories.dek: Iran reports civilian deaths including at a wedding. Hormuz control still the lever.
stories.caveman: The United States and Iran exchanged their heaviest blows since July. U.S. forces hit sites along Iran’s southern coast. Iran fired toward U.S. facilities in Jordan, Bahrain, Kuwait, and Iraq’s Erbil area. Tehran said civilians died, including people at a wedding. Talks remain stuck; Hormuz leverage is still central. Simple talk: the quiet pause broke, and the neighborhood got louder again.
stories.why_it_matters: More missiles mean higher oil, scared markets, and harder diplomacy.
stories.camps: Washington says pressure. Tehran says reciprocity. Gulf states want calm skies.

terms.explain: Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, a powerful military force.
Narrow waterway where a big share of world oil shipping passes.
A missile that flies a high arc and then falls on a target.
Many attacks launched in a short time.

stories.image_alt: Middle East crisis or military related scene

stories.headline: Kyiv hit for 7th straight day; at least 13 injured in central strikes
stories.dek: University, housing, medical site damaged. Zelensky flags new air-alert approach.
stories.caveman: Russian drones struck central Kyiv on Sept. 2, injuring at least 13 people and damaging a university, a residential building, and a medical facility, local officials said. It was the seventh straight day of heavy pressure on the capital. President Zelensky said Ukraine will change how air-raid alerts work. Simple talk: the city has not had a quiet morning all week.
stories.why_it_matters: A capital under nightly drones means more displacement, hospital strain, and harder peace talks.
stories.camps: Kyiv wants stronger air defenses. Moscow claims military aims. Civilians want sleep and shelters that work.

terms.explain: Siren or app warning that an attack may be coming.
Attack using unmanned aircraft carrying bombs.
The army branch that fights mostly on land.
The main government city — here, Kyiv.

stories.headline: Putin and Zelensky trade threats as drone war hits both sides
stories.dek: Zelensky warns foreign airlines about Russian airspace. Belgorod reports casualties.
stories.caveman: As drones and missiles flew, Vladimir Putin and Volodymyr Zelensky traded sharp threats. Zelensky warned foreign airlines that Russian skies are not safe because of Ukrainian long-range drones. Russia said it shot down many drones overnight; Belgorod officials reported dead and wounded from Ukrainian strikes. Simple talk: both leaders promise to raise the pain, while the front line stays mostly stuck.
stories.why_it_matters: Threats to airspace and energy sites can spill into global travel and oil markets.
stories.camps: Kyiv says pressure forces talks. Moscow vows retaliation. Airlines and insurers recalculate risk.

terms.explain: Unmanned aircraft that can fly far into another country.
The sky a country controls for planes.
A fight where neither side makes big land gains.
Hitting back after being hit.

stories.headline: Zelensky appoints new Ground Forces commander amid grinding war
stories.dek: Sviatoslav Zaiets replaces Hennadii Shapovalov, decree says.
stories.caveman: Ukraine’s president signed a Sept. 2 decree naming Sviatoslav Zaiets the new Ground Forces commander, replacing Hennadii Shapovalov. The change lands while Russia keeps pounding cities and Ukraine hits depots and air assets. Simple talk: when a long war stalls, leaders reshuffle the generals who run the land fight.
stories.why_it_matters: Command changes can shift tactics, morale, and Western confidence in Ukraine’s war plan.
stories.camps: Supporters call it renewal. Critics fear churn. Soldiers care if ammo and rotations improve.

terms.explain: The top officer in charge of a military branch.
An official order signed by the president.
A storage site for ammo or supplies.
Changing leaders or jobs inside an organization.

stories.headline: Robert Harris’s Agrippa hits U.S. shelves Sept. 1 — Rome on the edge of dictatorship
stories.dek: Doubleday. From the Conclave author; Wall Street Journal calls it a swift-paced romp.
stories.caveman: Robert Harris’s new novel Agrippa went on sale Sept. 1 in the United States. It follows Marcus Agrippa beside Octavius as Rome slides toward one-man rule. Reviews call it gripping and timely. Simple talk: a famous political thriller writer goes back to ancient Rome and makes power feel fresh.
stories.why_it_matters: Big September hardcovers set the fall reading list for U.S. bookstores and clubs.
stories.camps: History fans want accuracy. Thriller fans want pace. Teachers may assign the power lessons.

terms.explain: Roman general and friend of Augustus; also the novel’s title.
A book with a hard cover, usually the first fancy edition.
The day stores are allowed to sell a new book.
A story about power, plots, and danger in government.

stories.image_alt: Cover art for Agrippa by Robert Harris

stories.headline: Inaugural Black Bookstore Day draws crowds; coalition says it will return in 2027
stories.dek: Aug. 29 celebration honored Black-owned shops. Wichita founder: ‘y’all showed up.’
stories.caveman: The first Black Bookstore Day was held Saturday, Aug. 29. Founder Latasha Eley Kelly of Left on Read in Wichita said stores and readers showed up nationwide. The day honors Black-owned bookstores as community and literature hubs. Organizers already talk about 2027. Simple talk: a new annual holiday for Black bookstores just took its first victory lap.
stories.why_it_matters: Independent Black bookstores keep authors visible and neighborhoods stocked with stories schools skip.
stories.camps: Booksellers want year-round support, not one day. Readers celebrate belonging. Publishers watch sales lifts.

terms.explain: A locally owned book shop, not a giant chain.
A group of people or shops working together.
A public official statement recognizing a day or cause.
New books a store is pushing right now.

stories.image_alt: Black Bookstore Day logo or celebration

stories.headline: PW: The Poison Daughter debuts at No. 1 — and lands a Hulu series development deal
stories.dek: Sheila Masterson’s romantasy tops hardcover fiction on the Aug. 31 list.
stories.caveman: Publishers Weekly’s Aug. 31 bestsellers say Sheila Masterson’s The Poison Daughter debuted at No. 1 on the hardcover fiction list after Slowburn’s edition arrived with huge social buzz. PW also notes Hulu announced a series development deal in early August. Simple talk: a self-pub romantasy hit the top of the trade chart and Hollywood already wants TV rights.
stories.why_it_matters: Chart-toppers decide bookstore tables and what Hollywood shops next.
stories.camps: Romantasy readers celebrate. Traditional publishers hunt the next Masterson. TV fans wait for casting news.

terms.explain: Romance plus fantasy — love stories with magic or other worlds.
Weekly ranking of new hard novels by sales.
A studio pays to try turning a book into a show, not a finished series yet.
Author releases a book without a traditional publisher first.

stories.headline: September Indie Next List preview: booksellers tip fall fiction and essays
stories.dek: ABA flier highlights new staff picks for September shelves.
stories.caveman: The American Booksellers Association posted its September 2026 Indie Next List preview — 25 bookseller-loved titles plus paperback picks. The list is how indie shops tell shoppers what to read next after summer. Simple talk: local bookstores already voted on their fall favorites.
stories.why_it_matters: Indie Next placement can make a midlist novel suddenly visible across the U.S.
stories.camps: Authors chase the sticker. Booksellers defend taste. Big publishers watch which indies move.

terms.explain: Monthly list of books recommended by U.S. independent booksellers.
Trade group for indie bookstores.
A book a store worker personally recommends.
Books that are not mega-bestsellers but still matter.

stories.headline: Nepal flood toll passes 1,100; rescuers race for tunnel workers a week later
stories.dek: Nearly 4,000 still missing. China sending DNA experts and Bailey bridges.
stories.caveman: A week after a Himalayan glacier collapse sent flash floods through Nepal, authorities counted at least 1,114 dead and nearly 4,000 missing. Hopes for survivors elsewhere are fading, but teams still try to reach workers who may be alive inside hydropower tunnels. China said it will send more DNA experts and emergency gear. Simple talk: the clock is cruel, but tunnel air gives one last thin hope.
stories.why_it_matters: Climate-driven mountain disasters kill across borders and smash power and roads for months.
stories.camps: Families want names and bodies. Governments want bridges restored. Scientists say early warnings must improve.

terms.explain: A big chunk of ice and rock suddenly fails and falls.
Water rises very fast in a valley, often with little warning.
A quick-build temporary steel bridge used after disasters.
Using genetic tests to name unidentified victims.

stories.image_alt: Nepal flood rescue or Kathmandu relief

stories.headline: Indonesia’s Flores quake: nearly 190,000 still displaced; 111 dead
stories.dek: BNPB tally Aug. 30. Over 95,000 homes damaged; schools heavily hit.
stories.caveman: More than two weeks after a magnitude-7.7 quake hit Indonesia’s Flores region, about 188,000 people were still living away from home, the disaster agency said. The death toll stood at 111, with thousands injured and tens of thousands of homes wrecked. Aftershocks keep coming. Simple talk: the shaking stopped making headlines, but tents are still full.
stories.why_it_matters: Displacement this large needs months of shelter, school, and rebuild money — not just first-week rescue photos.
stories.camps: Local governments want temporary housing. Parents want schools back. Donors ask where aid goes.

terms.explain: People forced to leave home because of disaster or war.
A number that describes how strong an earthquake was.
Smaller quakes that follow a big one.
Indonesia’s national disaster management agency.

stories.headline: MSF: urgent needs linger three weeks after Colombia’s Aug. 10 quake
stories.dek: Mobile clinics in Buenaventura and Chocó. Conflict and weak services deepen gaps.
stories.caveman: Three weeks after a 7.4-magnitude earthquake hit western Colombia on Aug. 10, Doctors Without Borders says thousands still struggle for care, mental health help, food, and rebuild materials. Hardest gaps are in poor and conflict-hit areas like parts of Chocó and Buenaventura. Simple talk: when the cameras leave, the broken clinics stay broken.
stories.why_it_matters: Disasters hit unfairly. Places already hurt by violence need longer aid, not a one-week airlift.
stories.camps: MSF pushes mobile clinics. Local communities want rebuild materials. Officials face trust gaps.

terms.explain: A medical charity that works in crises.
Doctors and nurses who travel to treat people where hospitals are weak.
Help for fear, grief, and trauma after a disaster.
Colombian communities with African heritage, often under-served.

stories.headline: FEWS NET: South Sudan faces Emergency hunger and famine risk into 2027
stories.dek: Conflict, floods, and high prices. Some counties already see Catastrophe outcomes.
stories.caveman: A FEWS NET update warns that conflict and poor rains will keep Emergency-level hunger across much of South Sudan through the harvest and into early 2027. Millions need food help. In hard-to-reach parts of Jonglei and Upper Nile, some people already face Catastrophe. Simple talk: war plus weird weather means empty pots lasting months.
stories.why_it_matters: Famine risk is a policy alarm. Delayed aid becomes graves.
stories.camps: Aid groups want access. Armed actors block roads. Donors argue about funding cuts.

terms.explain: A U.S.-funded network that warns about hunger crises.
A 1-to-5 hunger scale. Higher numbers mean worse food insecurity.
Months when old harvest food runs out before new crops arrive.
Whether aid workers can safely reach people who need food and medicine.
